comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C16-C21 regarding the 44RKNR47 motif's role in CCL5-heparin interaction. Both evaluations find the mutant data, structural knowledge, and computational predictions well-supported. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on claims C44-C49 regarding gradient formation in cell-cell context. Both evaluations accept the microscopy data, HS-dependence via CHO cell comparison, and enhanced chemotaxis as solid evidence. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on claims C51-C54 regarding in vivo validation. Both evaluations affirm the mutant and competitive inhibition controls support the conclusion that phase separation drives chemotactic gradient formation in vivo. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on claims C60, C72-C74, C79-C80 representing the central mechanistic conclusions. Both evaluations explicitly affirm that phase separation driving chemotactic gradient formation is well-supported by converging evidence. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Divergent evaluations on claims C77-C78, C81-C82 regarding speculative hypotheses. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of direct experimental support, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting these as appropriately framed speculations for future investigation.

Strong agreement on claims C7-C15 regarding CCL5-heparin LLPS characterization. Both evaluations affirm the microscopy, FRAP, salt titration, and mutant analysis as solid evidence. OpenEval additionally includes C83-C85 (methodological and mechanistic context claims) not grouped by peer reviewers. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on claims C22-C27 regarding immobilization method comparison. Both evaluations accept the microscopy and 3D imaging data showing phase separation enables diffusion while direct binding does not. Peer review R3 also includes C28-C31 (Transwell chemotaxis data) which OpenEval groups separately in R4. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on claims C28-C31 regarding Transwell chemotaxis validation. OpenEval groups these separately from the immobilization comparison, while peer reviewers combine them with C22-C27. Both evaluations support the functional gradient interpretation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on claims C32-C36 regarding HS-dependent phase separation on CHO cell surfaces. OpenEval focuses on these claims specifically, while peer review R4 combines them with C37-C43 (functional validation with multiple controls). Both evaluations affirm the CHO-K1/CHO-677 comparison as central evidence. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on claims C37-C43 regarding comprehensive functional validation using Transwell assays with HS-deficient cells, competitive inhibition, and mutant controls. OpenEval groups these separately from C32-C36, while peer reviewers combine all cell-based GAG evidence. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on claim C50 regarding primary human blood cell migration. OpenEval also includes C87-C88 (methodological observations about variability) and notes this somewhat weakens quantitative interpretation. Peer reviewers accept the blood cell data without questioning variability. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Overlap on claims C87-C88 regarding experimental variability in primary cell experiments. OpenEval includes these with C50 and notes variability weakens interpretation, while peer reviewers treat them as unquestioned methodological observations. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on claims C1-C3, C5-C6 as established background literature about CCL5. OpenEval groups these as well-cited context, peer reviewers similarly accept without question. OpenEval also includes additional literature claims (C55-C56, C61-C63, C75, C89-C90) that peer reviewers group separately. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claim C4 regarding CCL5 oligomerization. OpenEval includes this with general background (R10), while peer reviewers specifically flag C4 and C67 as requiring additional discussion about the relationship between oligomerization and LLPS. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN while OpenEval's R10 is SUPPORTED.

Substantial overlap on literature context claims C55-C56, C61-C63, C75, C89-C90. Both evaluations treat these as established background knowledge that is appropriately cited. OpenEval groups broader literature context together, while peer reviewers separate by thematic content. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on claims C57-C59, C65-C66 regarding established LLPS concepts from literature. Both evaluations accept these as unquestioned background providing context for the study's approach. OpenEval also includes C84-C85 in R1. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on claims C68-C71, C76 as cited literature providing context. Both evaluations accept these background statements without challenge. OpenEval groups all literature context together while peer reviewers separate by topic. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claim C64 regarding knowledge gaps in chemokine-GAG-GPCR interactions. OpenEval includes this with general literature context, while peer reviewers highlight it separately to affirm the study's novelty. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claims C84-C85 regarding comparison to RNA-binding protein phase separation. OpenEval includes these with LLPS characterization (R1) as mechanistic context, while peer reviewers group with general LLPS literature concepts. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claim C83 regarding weak multivalent interactions. OpenEval includes this with LLPS characterization as supporting mechanistic interpretation, while peer reviewers treat as unquestioned methodological observation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claim C67 regarding oligomerization and LLPS relationship. OpenEval includes this with general literature context (R11, SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers specifically flag it with C4 as requiring additional discussion (R9, UNCERTAIN), indicating incomplete mechanistic evidence.
